sentence: Choose the transition that explicitly contrasts the location with the quiet inside.
setupText: The room faces a busy road. ___, it is quiet with the windows closed.
taskText: Choose the transition that explicitly contrasts the location with the quiet inside.
text: The room faces a busy road. ___, it is quiet with the windows closed. Choose the transition that explicitly contrasts the location with the quiet inside.
options: Therefore
For example
In addition
However
answer: However
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3741:However against a contextual expectation
explanation: However marks quiet inside as contrasting with the expectation created by a busy road.

rationales.However: However marks quiet inside as contrasting with the expectation created by a busy road.
rationales.Therefore: Therefore would present quiet as a result of facing the road.
rationales.For example: The quiet interior is not an example of the road's busyness.
rationales.In addition: In addition adds information without explicitly marking the requested contrast.

sentence: Which paraphrase preserves the connection?
setupText: The lift is out of order. Therefore, visitors must use the stairs.
taskText: Which paraphrase preserves the connection?
text: The lift is out of order. Therefore, visitors must use the stairs. Which paraphrase preserves the connection?
options: The lift stopped because visitors used the stairs.
Visitors must use the stairs before the lift stops.
The lift is working, but visitors prefer the stairs.
Visitors must use the stairs because the lift is not working.
answer: Visitors must use the stairs because the lift is not working.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3742:Recasting a result link as a reason clause
explanation: Therefore presents stair use as the consequence of the broken lift; because can express the same link in reverse sentence order.

rationales.The lift stopped because visitors used t: This reverses the stated reason and result.
rationales.Visitors must use the stairs because the: Therefore presents stair use as the consequence of the broken lift; because can express the same link in reverse sentence order.
rationales.Visitors must use the stairs before the: This introduces an earlier-time requirement instead of the stated consequence.
rationales.The lift is working, but visitors prefer: That changes both the lift's condition and obligation into preference.

sentence: What does 'for example' tell us about the two activities?
setupText: Several evening activities are available, for example, pottery and photography.
taskText: What does 'for example' tell us about the two activities?
text: Several evening activities are available, for example, pottery and photography. What does 'for example' tell us about the two activities?
options: They are two examples of the activities offered.
They are the complete list of available activities.
They are reasons for cancelling the evening program.
They must be taken in the order listed.
answer: They are two examples of the activities offered.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3743:Examples versus an exhaustive list
explanation: For example introduces selected members of a wider group without closing the list.

rationales.They are the complete list of available: For example gives instances, not necessarily an exhaustive list.
rationales.They are reasons for cancelling the even: They illustrate the activities offered, not cancellation reasons.
rationales.They are two examples of the activities: For example introduces selected members of a wider group without closing the list.
An example marker does not set a timetable.

sentence: Choose the transition that adds another advantage without suggesting a cause.
setupText: The flat is near my workplace. ___, the rent includes heating.
taskText: Choose the transition that adds another advantage without suggesting a cause.
text: The flat is near my workplace. ___, the rent includes heating. Choose the transition that adds another advantage without suggesting a cause.
options: As a result
In addition
Instead
However
answer: In addition
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3744:Adding parallel reasons for a choice
explanation: In addition places included heating alongside location as another benefit.

rationales.As a result: Proximity is not presented as causing heating to be included.
rationales.Instead: The second advantage does not replace the first.
rationales.However: However marks opposition, not the requested addition of an advantage.
rationales.In addition: In addition places included heating alongside location as another benefit.

sentence: What does 'instead' connect the cafe meal to?
setupText: We planned to cook at home. The kitchen tap broke, so we ate at a cafe instead.
taskText: What does 'instead' connect the cafe meal to?
text: We planned to cook at home. The kitchen tap broke, so we ate at a cafe instead. What does 'instead' connect the cafe meal to?
options: The repair of the kitchen tap
The plan to cook at home
A second meal after cooking at home
The reason the tap broke
answer: The plan to cook at home
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3745:Recovering the replaced plan with instead
explanation: Instead identifies the cafe meal as the alternative to the earlier plan.

rationales.The plan to cook at home: Instead identifies the cafe meal as the alternative to the earlier plan.
rationales.The repair of the kitchen tap: The meal replaces cooking, not the act of repairing the tap.
rationales.A second meal after cooking at home: Instead marks replacement, not an additional meal.
rationales.The reason the tap broke: The transition does not explain the breakage.

sentence: Which word presents enjoyment as contrasting with tiredness?
setupText: ___ I was tired after work, I enjoyed the evening walk.
taskText: Which word presents enjoyment as contrasting with tiredness?
text: ___ I was tired after work, I enjoyed the evening walk. Which word presents enjoyment as contrasting with tiredness?
options: Although
Because
Before
If
answer: Although
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3746:Although with a conceded actual circumstance
explanation: Although concedes tiredness while introducing an outcome that contrasts with it.

rationales.Because: Because would present tiredness as the reason for enjoyment.
rationales.Although: Although concedes tiredness while introducing an outcome that contrasts with it.
rationales.Before: Before gives a time relationship rather than the specified contrast.
rationales.If: If makes tiredness a condition instead of presenting it as a fact.

sentence: Which question does the because-clause answer?
setupText: 'I emailed because the booking date was wrong.'
taskText: Which question does the because-clause answer?
text: 'I emailed because the booking date was wrong.' Which question does the because-clause answer?
options: What did the email change?
When did the email arrive?
Who made the incorrect booking?
Why did the speaker email?
answer: Why did the speaker email?
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3747:Reason clause versus action outcome
explanation: Because introduces the wrong date as the reason for emailing.

rationales.What did the email change?: The clause gives the reason for writing, not the result achieved.
rationales.When did the email arrive?: It does not identify a delivery time.
rationales.Why did the speaker email?: Because introduces the wrong date as the reason for emailing.
rationales.Who made the incorrect booking?: The clause does not identify who made the error.

sentence: Which version keeps the required order of actions?
setupText: Check the delivery address before you confirm the order.
taskText: Which version keeps the required order of actions?
text: Check the delivery address before you confirm the order. Which version keeps the required order of actions?
options: Check the address while you are confirming the order.
Before confirming the order, check the delivery address.
Confirm the order so that you can check the address.
Check the address because you confirmed the order.
answer: Before confirming the order, check the delivery address.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3748:Before with a clause or an -ing phrase
explanation: Before plus confirming keeps the check earlier than confirmation, just as the original clause does.

rationales.Check the address while you are confirmi: While permits overlap rather than requiring the check beforehand.
rationales.Confirm the order so that you can check: This reverses the practical sequence and introduces a purpose.
rationales.Check the address because you confirmed: That makes confirmation already completed and gives a reason instead.
rationales.Before confirming the order, check the d: Before plus confirming keeps the check earlier than confirmation, just as the original clause does.

sentence: What timing does 'after' establish?
setupText: After the library reopened, I renewed my membership.
taskText: What timing does 'after' establish?
text: After the library reopened, I renewed my membership. What timing does 'after' establish?
options: Renewal happened the instant the doors opened.
Renewal caused the reopening.
Renewal came later than reopening.
Renewal and reopening began together.
answer: Renewal came later than reopening.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3749:Later timing without an immediacy claim
explanation: After orders the events but does not by itself say how soon renewal followed.

After orders the events but does not by itself say how soon renewal followed.
rationales.Renewal happened the instant the doors o: Immediate timing would need a stronger expression such as as soon as.
A time sequence does not itself express that causal claim.
After puts renewal later rather than at the same starting point.

sentence: Choose the word that makes collecting the keys the end of the wait.
setupText: Wait here ___ I collect the keys. Then we can go upstairs.
taskText: Choose the word that makes collecting the keys the end of the wait.
text: Wait here ___ I collect the keys. Then we can go upstairs. Choose the word that makes collecting the keys the end of the wait.
options: until
because
although
after
answer: until
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3750:Until linking duration to an endpoint
explanation: Until makes key collection the boundary up to which the waiting continues.

rationales.because: Because would give a reason, not specify the wait's endpoint.
rationales.until: Until makes key collection the boundary up to which the waiting continues.
rationales.although: Although would contrast waiting with collecting rather than time the endpoint.
rationales.after: After would place waiting later than collection, reversing the intended sequence.

sentence: Which situation directly activates this instruction?
setupText: The invitation says, 'If you need a parking space, email the organizer.'
taskText: Which situation directly activates this instruction?
text: The invitation says, 'If you need a parking space, email the organizer.' Which situation directly activates this instruction?
options: You have already returned your parking permit.
You need somewhere to park for the event.
You want to know the organizer's name.
You have decided not to attend the event.
answer: You need somewhere to park for the event.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3751:Applying a conditional instruction to a situation
explanation: If links the request to email with the need for a parking space; it does not say that this need definitely exists.

rationales.You have already returned your parking p: The instruction concerns needing a space, not returning a permit.
That need is not the condition specified.
rationales.You need somewhere to park for the event: If links the request to email with the need for a parking space; it does not say that this need definitely exists.
rationales.You have decided not to attend the event: Nonattendance is not the stated condition for this request.

sentence: What relationship does 'so that' express here?
setupText: I wrote the number in large letters so that my father could read it.
taskText: What relationship does 'so that' express here?
text: I wrote the number in large letters so that my father could read it. What relationship does 'so that' express here?
options: His reading caused the large writing.
His being able to read it was the purpose.
Large letters are an example of his reading.
He read it before the writing was finished.
answer: His being able to read it was the purpose.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3752:So that expressing intended benefit
explanation: So that plus could expresses the intended result of writing large letters; purpose does not by itself prove success.

This reverses the direction and treats the intended benefit as an earlier cause.
rationales.Large letters are an example of his read: The second clause gives the intended benefit, not an example.
rationales.He read it before the writing was finish: The sentence does not establish that timing.
rationales.His being able to read it was the purpos: So that plus could expresses the intended result of writing large letters; purpose does not by itself prove success.

sentence: Which action should happen after passing the pharmacy?
setupText: The map says, 'Go past the pharmacy. Then take the first left.'
taskText: Which action should happen after passing the pharmacy?
text: The map says, 'Go past the pharmacy. Then take the first left.' Which action should happen after passing the pharmacy?
options: Turning left before reaching the pharmacy
Stopping inside the pharmacy
Taking the first left
Returning to the previous junction
answer: Taking the first left
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3753:Then advancing spatial directions
explanation: Then advances the route from the landmark to the turn.

rationales.Taking the first left: Then advances the route from the landmark to the turn.
rationales.Turning left before reaching the pharmac: This puts the turn before the landmark instead of after it.
rationales.Stopping inside the pharmacy: Passing a landmark does not instruct entry.
rationales.Returning to the previous junction: Then advances the directions; it does not send the traveler back.

sentence: Which interpretation preserves 'such as'?
setupText: Please bring a warm item, such as a sweater.
taskText: Which interpretation preserves 'such as'?
text: Please bring a warm item, such as a sweater. Which interpretation preserves 'such as'?
options: A sweater is required in addition to a warm item.
A sweater is unsuitable for this purpose.
A sweater is one suitable example.
Only a sweater meets the request.
answer: A sweater is one suitable example.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3754:Such as linking a category to a noun-phrase example
explanation: Such as introduces an example; another suitable warm item may also meet the request.

rationales.A sweater is required in addition to a w: The sweater is a member of the warm-item category, not an extra category.
Such as introduces an example; another suitable warm item may also meet the request.
rationales.A sweater is unsuitable for this purpose: The phrase offers it as suitable, not excluded.
Such as does not make the example an exhaustive requirement.

sentence: How does 'besides' link the final point?
setupText: 'Let's take the train. Parking is expensive. Besides, I don't want to drive tonight.'
taskText: How does 'besides' link the final point?
text: 'Let's take the train. Parking is expensive. Besides, I don't want to drive tonight.' How does 'besides' link the final point?
options: It explains why parking prices increased.
It replaces the concern about parking.
It adds another reason to take the train.
It gives an example of expensive parking.
answer: It adds another reason to take the train.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3755:Besides adding a supporting reason
explanation: Besides introduces a further supporting reason, here a preference against driving.

rationales.It explains why parking prices increased: The speaker's preference does not explain the parking price.
The preference adds to the cost concern rather than withdrawing it.
rationales.It adds another reason to take the train: Besides introduces a further supporting reason, here a preference against driving.
rationales.It gives an example of expensive parking: A wish not to drive is not an example of a parking price.

sentence: When is the suggested waiting period?
setupText: The mechanic is inspecting the car. In the meantime, you can wait in the lounge.
taskText: When is the suggested waiting period?
text: The mechanic is inspecting the car. In the meantime, you can wait in the lounge. When is the suggested waiting period?
options: Before the mechanic starts the inspection
Only after the car is ready
During the inspection
At the next scheduled inspection
answer: During the inspection
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3756:In the meantime filling an ongoing interval
explanation: In the meantime introduces an activity in the interval occupied by another ongoing event.

rationales.Before the mechanic starts the inspectio: In the meantime refers to the period while the inspection is taking place.
rationales.Only after the car is ready: That would be after the waiting period described.
rationales.At the next scheduled inspection: The suggestion concerns the current inspection, not a later appointment.
rationales.During the inspection: In the meantime introduces an activity in the interval occupied by another ongoing event.

sentence: What does 'finally' mark here?
setupText: The message explains where to park and which entrance to use. It ends, 'Finally, please bring a photo ID.'
taskText: What does 'finally' mark here?
text: The message explains where to park and which entrance to use. It ends, 'Finally, please bring a photo ID.' What does 'finally' mark here?
options: The last point in the message
The last action to perform after entering
A result caused by the parking instructions
A correction to the entrance information
answer: The last point in the message
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3757:Text order versus real-world action order
explanation: Finally can close a list of instructions without saying the real-world action must happen last.

rationales.The last point in the message: Finally can close a list of instructions without saying the real-world action must happen last.
rationales.The last action to perform after enterin: The text position alone does not make bringing ID an action after entry.
rationales.A result caused by the parking instructi: The ID request is another point, not an effect of parking advice.
rationales.A correction to the entrance information: Nothing retracts or changes the entrance instructions.

sentence: Which connection does 'while' make in this sentence?
setupText: I listened to the radio while I cooked dinner.
taskText: Which connection does 'while' make in this sentence?
text: I listened to the radio while I cooked dinner. Which connection does 'while' make in this sentence?
options: The two activities overlapped in time.
Cooking finished before the listening began.
The radio caused the decision to cook.
The speaker chose listening instead of cooking.
answer: The two activities overlapped in time.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3758:Temporal overlap without exact matching boundaries
explanation: While connects the listening with the period spent cooking; their starting and ending times need not match exactly.

rationales.Cooking finished before the listening be: While places listening during cooking, not wholly after it.
While connects the listening with the period spent cooking; their starting and ending times need not match exactly.
The sentence links time rather than giving a cause.
rationales.The speaker chose listening instead of c: While allows both activities rather than replacing one with the other.

sentence: Which version preserves the stated plan and exception?
setupText: We will use the terrace unless it rains.
taskText: Which version preserves the stated plan and exception?
text: We will use the terrace unless it rains. Which version preserves the stated plan and exception?
options: We will use the terrace only when it rains.
We will use the terrace because it is raining.
We will use the terrace after the rain begins.
If it does not rain, we will use the terrace.
answer: If it does not rain, we will use the terrace.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3759:Unless as an exception to a plan
explanation: Unless introduces the rain exception; if it does not rain preserves the stated default plan.

rationales.We will use the terrace only when it rai: This makes rain the condition for terrace use instead of the exception.
rationales.We will use the terrace because it is ra: Rain becomes an actual reason, which changes the conditional plan.
rationales.If it does not rain, we will use the ter: Unless introduces the rain exception; if it does not rain preserves the stated default plan.
rationales.We will use the terrace after the rain b: That changes the exception into a starting time.

sentence: Which summary preserves the link made by 'as well'?
setupText: The course includes conversation practice. It offers pronunciation work as well.
taskText: Which summary preserves the link made by 'as well'?
text: The course includes conversation practice. It offers pronunciation work as well. Which summary preserves the link made by 'as well'?
options: Pronunciation work replaces conversation practice.
Conversation practice is an example of pronunciation work.
Pronunciation work happens only after conversation practice.
Both conversation and pronunciation are included.
answer: Both conversation and pronunciation are included.
focusKey: coverage-transitions-a2-3760:Recovering the earlier member of an additive pair
explanation: As well links pronunciation as another included component alongside conversation practice.

rationales.Pronunciation work replaces conversation: As well adds pronunciation rather than replacing the first activity.
rationales.Conversation practice is an example of p: The text presents two components, not one as an example of the other.
rationales.Pronunciation work happens only after co: As well does not set their time order.
rationales.Both conversation and pronunciation are: As well links pronunciation as another included component alongside conversation practice.
